sentences.text:
Respondent :- State Of U.P. And 4 Others Counsel for Petitioner :- Vinayak Mithal Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.,Vineet Pandey,Vivek Saran Hon'ble Mrs. Sunita Agarwal,J.
Hon'ble Vikas Budhwar,J.
Heard Sri Rakesh Pandey learned Senior Counsel assisted by Sri Vinayak Mittal and Sri Rajiv Giri,
learned counsels for the petitioners and Sri Vivek Saran learned Advocate for U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad.
Learned Standing Counsel appears for the State respondents.

At the very outset, Sri Vivek Saran, learned Advocate appearing for U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad has invited the attention of the Court to the application dated 03.09.2022 wherein it is indicated that the petitioners No. 2 and 3 had entered into an agreement with the U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad and have executed sale deeds to transfer their land holdings in its favour.
They have also agreed to withdraw the litigations initiated by them.
The copy of the affidavits given by petitioners No. 2 and 3 before the Parishad, are appended with the said affidavit.

This fact is not disputed by the Mahesh Chandra Gautam And 4 Others vs State Of U.P. And 4 Others on 14 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62370270/
1 learned counsel for the petitioners by filing any objection to the said affidavit, copy of which was served upon the counsel for the petitioners on 31.10.2022.

sentences.text: For the aforesaid, we dismiss the writ petition on behalf of the petitioners No. 2 and 3 as having become infructuous.

With regard to the remaining petitioners No. 1, 4 and 5 and the petitioners in the connected writ petitions, we may note that the dispute raised in the present bunch of writ petitions is about the circle rate determined by the Collector, District Mathura in the year 2016-17.

While pressing the abovenoted prayers of challenge to the determination of the circle rate by the Collector, District Mathura, it is submitted by the learned Senior Advocate appearing for the petitioners that an illusory distinction has been drawn by the District Collector while determining different circle rates for different plot numbers of the same village in the year 2015.
A copy of Form '4' Kha showing the circle rate of the lands of village Alhepur (subject matter of concern) from the year 2008 till 2016 has been appended from pages '33' to '41' of the writ petition.

Placing our attention to the said documents, it is pointed out by the learned Senior Counsel for the petitioners that the determination of circle rate for two different categories of lands, Bamba Ki Patri (Chhatikara-Charaura) and Bamba Ki Patri (Alhepur to Tehra), indicated therein with the plot numbers mentioned in the Form 4Ka, was included with a view to deprive the land holders of just and adequate compensation, which was required to be determined as on 01.01.2014, the date of enforcement of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

sentences.text: It is an admitted fact that the acquisition notifications under Section 28 and 32 of U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad Adhiniyam, 1965 had been published in the year 2006 and 2010.

entities.text: U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad Adhiniyam, 1965
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: No award for the acquired land had been declared.

A perusal of the Board Meeting of Avas Evam Vikas Parishad at page '50' of the paper book further indicates that an effort was made to enter into negotiations with the land holders in the year 2016, in accordance with the provisions of the Government Order dated 21.03.2016, wherein a direction was issued by the State Government to determine compensation with the consent of the tenure holders at the current circle rate, in case where no award had been made.
It was resolved by the Board of U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad to provide compensation to the petitioners at the circle rate prevailing in the year 2016, determined by the Collector.

entities.text: Board of U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: At that stage, the petitioners raised objection with regard to the determination of compensation by the Collector by creation of two additional categories of lands with their plot numbers in the notification for determination of the circle rate.

On account of the dispute raised by the petitioners about determination of the circle rate by the Collector, in the year 2016, the computation of compensation for the acquired land could not be finalized nor compensation could be paid to the petitioners.

The writ petitions in this bunch has been filed in the year 2020 with the above noted prayers to quash the circle rate determined by the Collector in the year 2016-17 and issue a writ of mandamus commanding the District Collector to revise the circle rate of the petitioners' land.

We find fallacy in the first two prayers made by the petitioners in the present bunch of writ petitions seeking a writ in the nature of certiorari for quashing and direction in the nature of mandamus commanding the District Magistrate to revise the circle rate on the premise that circle rates of two different categories of plots have been determined by the Collector in the year 2014, illegally, just to deprive the petitioners tenure holders of their right to receive just compensation.

Noticing the submission of the learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioners and having perused the documents of determination of circle rate from the year 2008 till 2016, we find that with the passage of time, there has been development of the area in question namely, village Alhepur and two additional categories of circle rate had been added by the Collector in the year 2014, indicating the number of plots abetting the roads created on account of the development.
The additional two categories of lands have been created for village Alhepur in the year 2014, which seems to us, was a result of development of the area in question.

The determination of circle rate in the year 2014 for various categories of lands of village Alhepur had not been revised till 2016 and the revision in the year 2016 are of only for two categories making them effective since 11.09.2015,
which were added in the circle rate determined in the year 2014.

In any case, the challenge to the determination made by the Collector on 06.07.2016 for two categories noted above, cannot be sustained for the simple reason that the petitioners cannot be said to have been discriminated for creation of different categories of lands for determination of circle rate.
No good ground has been made out to challenge the circle rate determined by the Collector for two categories created in the year 2014 with effect from 11.09.2015 by the order dated 06.07.2016.
Even otherwise, the determination of circle rate is a pure function of the executive as it depends upon various factors which are to be taken into account by the Collector.
There is no challenge to the procedure adopted by the Collector.

The process of judicial review in executive function is limited to the decision Mahesh Chandra Gautam And 4 Others vs State Of U.P. And 4 Others on 14 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62370270/
3 making process and not the decision itself.

sentences.text: The prayer made in the writ petition to command the District Magistrate Mathura to revise the circle rate of the land in question without laying any foundation for the challenge in the present writ petition, therefore, cannot be entertained.

Further, the dispute essentially in the writ petitions is about the determination of compensation for the land acquired by the notifications issued in the year 2006/2010 under U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad Adhiniyam, 1965.

entities.text: U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad Adhiniyam, 1965
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
The record further indicates that the committee constituted under the Government Order dated 21.03.2016 had held a meeting on 26.05.2018 for the purpose of determination of the compensation for the lands of village Alhepur wherein the land in question,
belonging to the petitioners, is situate.
A decision was taken to pay compensation to the land holders in accordance with the Government Order dated 21.03.2016, at the circle rate prevailing in the year 2016-17.

The said decision of the committee was accepted by the Board of U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad in its meeting held on 9th October, 2019, and the exercise for entering into an agreement with the land holders had been initiated.

It is evident from the record that the petitioners raising a dispute with regard to the determination of circle rate by the Collector did not accept the offer given by the U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad for compensation.

An alternative prayer has been made in the writ petitions to issue a direction to the Competent Authority namely, Special Land Acquisition Officer for making an award in accordance with the provisions of Section 24(1)(a) of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Considering the prayer made in the writ petition and the stand of U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad that they are agreeable to pay compensation to the petitioners for the acquired land as per the prevailing rules in the year 2016, we are of the considered opinion that the petitioners are at liberty to accept the rates fixed by the U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad and in case of any denial on the part of the petitioners to enter into an agreement with the U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad, it would be incumbent upon the U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad to approach the Special Land Acquisition Officer asking him to determine the compensation, strictly in accordance with the provisions of Section 24(1)(a) of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: In any case, the proceeding for determination of compensation for the acquired land by consent or by making an award by the Special Land Acquisition Officer, in accordance with the provisions of Section 24(1)(a) of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013,

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013

sentences.text: shall be completed within a period of three months from the date of receipt of the copy of this order.
Subject to the above observations and directions, all the writ petitions in this bunch, are disposed of.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Considering the prayer made in the writ petition and the stand of U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad that they are agreeable to pay compensation to the petitioners for the acquired land as per the prevailing rules in the year 2016, we are of the considered opinion that the petitioners are at liberty to accept the rates fixed by the U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad and in case of any denial on the part of the petitioners to enter into an agreement with the U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad, it would be incumbent upon the U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad to approach the Special Land Acquisition Officer asking him to determine the compensation, strictly in accordance with the provisions of Section 24(1)(a) of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
In any case, the proceeding for determination of compensation for the acquired land by consent or by making an award by the Special Land Acquisition Officer, in accordance with the provisions of Section 24(1)(a) of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013,
shall be completed within a period of three months from the date of receipt of the copy of this order.
Subject to the above observations and directions, all the writ petitions in this bunch, are disposed of.
